thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED: Sev 2 - routing anomalies detected - service: routing-proxy - region: na-east-1 - alerts: spike in 500s and tail latency. Pager: emily (oncall).
emily (oncall): On it. Can someone post the initial metrics and which model groups are affected?
raj (infra): Seeing a sustained 3x increase in routing queue length on na-east-1 gateways starting ~2051234200. Autoscaler triggered capacity additions but we saw repeated evictions.
zoe (sre): Customer-facing symptom: some requests got 502/504 from proxy; a smaller subset saw 200 but with 2-3x latency. Topology shows traffic spilling to na-west-1 for heavy sessions.
sara (runtime): The routing policy should have fallen back to "lm-small-quant" for low tiers, but logs show requests routed to "lm-large-v2" in some cases (mismatch with tier policy). Possible policy mis-eval or config drift.
nikhil (product): Are enterprise customers affected? Any SLA breaches?
emily (oncall): Preliminary: 10 enterprise orgs reported increased latency, 3 reported errors; not yet SLA breach but could escalate.
logs-bot: Attached logs: https://logs.redwood/stream/2051234567?a=proxy&b=route-eval (redacted)
raj (infra): Pasting key snippets (sanitized):
```
2026-07-01T12:03:15Z [proxy] route_eval id=abcd tier=standard selected_variant=lm-large-v2 fallback_policy=quantized-first reason=cache-miss
2026-07-01T12:03:15Z [router] enqueue id=abcd node=na-east-1 queue_len=120
2026-07-01T12:03:16Z [serving] dispatch id=abcd shard=hot-3 evict=true err=capacity_exceeded
2026-07-01T12:03:17Z [proxy] upstream_error id=abcd code=502
```
zoe (sre): Important: note the `evict=true` and `shard=hot-3` lines - suggests hot-shard eviction leading to request spillover.
sara (runtime): Hypothesis A: Hot-shard eviction due to memory pressure on GPU nodes caused routing to overspill into fallback selection path which erroneously picked a higher-capacity model variant because of a stale model-compat map.
raj (infra): Hypothesis B: Autoscaler scaled nodes but kept older model bundles active; route-eval cache contained entries mapping to large variants. Cache invalidation failed during scale events.
emily (oncall): Can we get counts per model variant for the spike window?
logs-bot: Query results: `lm-large-v2: 18k requests, lm-small-quant: 4k requests, lm-medium: 7k` for 2051234200-2051234500
nikhil (product): That's consistent with misroutes to large variant. Larger models consumed GPU and caused evictions -> feedback loop.
sara (runtime): Immediate mitigation I propose: 1) Disable cross-region spillover for na-east-1 (force local routing), 2) Temporarily pin fallback to `lm-small-quant` for tier=standard via policy override, 3) Bump route-eval cache TTL to 30s and trigger manual invalidate.
emily (oncall): Execute mitigations. Raj/Zoe help with infra steps, Sara handle routing policy change.
raj (infra): Running command to disable spillover (dry-run):
```
# disable regional overflow
redwoodctl routing set-policy --region na-east-1 --allow-spillover false --commit
```
raj (infra): Applied. Confirming no new spill events in last 60s.
sara (runtime): Patching tier policy:
```
# force fallback for standard tier
redwoodctl policy set --tier standard --fallback lm-small-quant --force
```
sara (runtime): Applied. Also invalidated route-eval cache: `redwoodctl cache invalidate --scope route-eval --region na-east-1`
zoe (sre): Monitoring: error rate dropping from 6.2% to 1.1% over 2 min; p95 latency back to ~180ms from 580ms.
emily (oncall): Good. Start timeline notes for RCA: root window 2051234200-2051234800. Assign tasks: logs + heap dumps (raj), model-compat table diff (sara), autoscaler event trace (zoe), customer impact list (nikhil).
raj (infra): Uploaded node traces: https://logs.redwood/nodes/trace-2051234567 (sanitized). Observed increased OOM-kill attempts on nodes labeled `gpu-na-east-hot-*`.
sara (runtime): Model-compat map diff shows that a config push at 2051234155 introduced an entry mapping `tier=standard, workload=embed` -> `lm-large-v2` for legacy reasons. That push also had a failed partial rollout.
nikhil (product): So a config push + hot shard eviction + cache TTL = perfect storm. We should track the config push author and rollout id.
emily (oncall): Who did the config push?
sara (runtime): It was `deploy-bot` triggered by `ci/1254` but rollout was aborted due to an unrelated test failure. The partial state remained in the config-store.
raj (infra): Replaying timeline: 2051234155 config push -> 2051234200 routing traffic increases -> 2051234230 autoscaler events -> 2051234250 shard evictions -> 2051234270 spillover -> 2051234300 customer reports and paging.
zoe (sre): Add hypothesis C: Partial config rollouts can leave a transient inconsistent policy surface between route-eval caches and config-store which leads to misroutes.
emily (oncall): Action items now:
- Short-term (mitigated): Confirmed mitigations live, monitoring stable. (owners: raj/sara)
- Mid-term: Add safer config rollback semantics and ensure aborted rollouts clean up mappings. (owner: sara + infra)
- Long-term: Improve autoscaler grace to avoid immediate eviction of hot shards, and add routing circuit-breaker when eviction rate > threshold. (owner: zoe + raj)
- Customer comms: Nikil to draft note for affected orgs with timeline and mitigation.
nikhil (product): Will draft. ETA 1h.
emily (oncall): Handoff: I'll leave a post-incident task list and hand off monitoring to Zoe for the next 4h. If metrics re-regress, page the oncall.
zoe (sre): A few more artifacts: heap dumps (link), route-eval cache state at spike, and the problematic config diff are in the RCA folder: https://docs.redwood/incidents/2051234567/rca-artifacts
sara (runtime): For the RCA note, I'll enumerate the causal chain and include mitigation PRs: - prevent partial-config-to-route mismatch - ensure cache invalidation on partial rollouts - add model-compat verification in CI.
emily (oncall): Closing live triage. Creating formal RCA ticket now and assigning to owners above. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
nikhil (product): Confirmed customers notified, sent initial heads-up.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity downgraded to S3.
emily (oncall): Logging final summary in timeline doc and moving thread to follow-up.
(END OF THREAD)
